title: [YouPass Collect] - Energy sources in Australia
prompt: The pie charts show energy sources in Australia in 2008 and predictions for 2030. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The charts give information about energy generation from different sources in 2008, while making projections for the year 2030.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, despite some changes, Australia is predicted to continue relying mainly on non-renewable sources over the 22-year period. Coal, oil, and gas will still make up the largest parts of energy production, while renewable sources, even with some growth, especially the appearance of geothermal energy, are expected to remain a small part of the total.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding the major sources, coal accounted for the largest share at 39%, followed by oil at 32.5% and gas at 22.9%. By 2030, oil consumption is forecast to increase slightly to 35.5%, becoming the most dominant energy source. Similarly, gas usage is expected to grow significantly to 32%, representing nearly a third of all energy production by 2030. Coal usage is projected to fall dramatically to 22.3%, making it the third most used energy source among fossil fuels.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding alternative energy sources, these collectively constituted a very small proportion in 2008, with solar, wind, and hydro accounting for merely 0.8%, 0.3%, and 0.2% respectively, while "others" made up 4.3%. By 2030, wind and hydro energy are predicted to see modest growth to 0.9% and 0.7%, while solar energy is not specifically listed in the 2030 projection. Most notably, geothermal energy, which was not recorded as a separate category in 2008, will contribute 4.3% of energy production by 2030, equal to the "others" category, which remains unchanged throughout the period.
